In square units rounded to one decimal place, the area of $△ABC$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m∠B={72}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠B,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘}) & =\frac{3x+4}{2x-1} \\ (2x-1)\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘}) & =3x+4 \\ 2x\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘})-\operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘}) & =3x+4 \\ x(2\operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘})-3) & =4+\operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘}) \\ x & =\frac{4+\operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘})}{2\operatorname{tan}⁡({72}^{∘})-3} \\ x & =2.243\,0…\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =2x-1=2(2.243\,0…)-1=3.486\,1…, \\ AC & =3x+4=3(2.243\,0…)+4=10.729\,1….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}(10.729\,1…)(3.486\,1…) \\  & =18.701\,3… \\  & ≈18.7,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
